issue_context.title: Lock reversal leading to potential dead lock or recursive lock call in provider_init()
issue_context.body:
This appeared in Coverity scan:

The provider_init() acquires a write lock for the prov->flag lock and then tries to acquire read lock on get_provider_store()->lock to obtain the store->default_path.

Where in provider_activate_fallbacks() a write lock on store->lock is acquired and then provider_activate() is called which calls provider_init() as well and if that succeeds it tries to acquire write lock on prov->flag_lock.

We probable have to have a special lock for the default_path.

There is also a bug in that when the store->default_path is read in provider_init(), it is not strdup-ed under the lock meaning that use-after-free will happen if OSSL_PROVIDER_set_default_search_path() is called simultaneously - i.e. the read lock on the store->lock currently does not really fix the race condition it was supposed to cover.

review_comments: Where/when will this allocation be released ?
You're missing `CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock(store->default_path_lock);` unlock call in case `store->default_path == NULL`
